newsitem.title: USA: May same-store retail sales rise 2.3 pct - Telecheck.
newsitem.headline: May same-store retail sales rise 2.3 pct - Telecheck.

text.p: May same-store retail spending rose a moderate 2.3 percent over the same period last year, according to data compiled by TeleCheck Services Inc.
According to Telecheck, the Southeast led with a 3.3 percent sales gain, the West had a 3.0 percent gain, Mid-Atlantic sales grew 2.9 percent and sales rose 2.5 percent in the Midwest.
The Southwest's sales gained 2.0 percent, while the Northeast's fell 1.1 percent.

"May same-store sales growth is consistent with an economy that is still growing, but at a slower rate than in the first quarter. Although the pace of economic growth has slowed, consumer confidence is strong and unemployment rates remain low," said William Ford, TeleCheck's senior economic advisor, in a press release.
"Same-store sales received a boost from a calendar fluctuation, in which this May had one more Saturday than last," he said.

The TeleCheck Retail Index is based on a year-over-year, same-store comparison of the dollar volume of checks written by consumers at more than 27,000 of TeleCheck's 167,000 subscribing locations. Figures are not adjusted for inflation.
TeleCheck, a subsidiary of First Data Corp, said checks account for about 37 percent of retail spending.
